stories.title: Cerebras shares plummet 16% after results fail to impress investors
stories.simple_summary: A company called Cerebras that makes AI computer chips saw its stock price drop sharply because its financial results disappointed the people who own shares in it.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors in that company — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Amazon will train on Twitch streamers’ content by default, unless they opt out
stories.simple_summary: Amazon is planning to use videos from Twitch streamers (people who broadcast themselves playing games or doing other activities online) to train its AI, unless the streamers specifically say no first.
stories.why_it_matters: If you stream on Twitch, you should check your settings and opt out if you don't want your content used this way.

stories.title: AI was supposed to destroy jobs. Where’s the carnage?
stories.simple_summary: The headline asks why AI hasn't caused massive job losses yet, when many people predicted it would.
stories.why_it_matters: So far, AI hasn't put people out of work as dramatically as feared — though this could change as the technology improves.

stories.title: AI coding startup Cognition reportedly already in talks to raise at $40B valuation
stories.simple_summary: A startup company that makes AI tools for writing computer code is trying to raise a lot of money at a very high value, just a few months after raising money before.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: As AI safety concerns mount, three pioneers make the case for staying open
stories.simple_summary: Major AI experts are debating whether AI companies should keep their technology open for anyone to use, or keep it more controlled, and how America should compete with other countries.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to policymakers and tech companies — nothing you need to act on right now.

stories.title: OpenAI-backed Thrive Holdings raises $2B to bring AI to the enterprise
stories.simple_summary: A company called Thrive Holdings, which has backing from OpenAI, raised a large amount of money to sell AI tools to businesses.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Twitch streamers can now opt out from training Amazon’s AI
stories.simple_summary: Twitch streamers now have the option to prevent Amazon from using their videos and chat messages to train its AI systems.
stories.why_it_matters: If you stream on Twitch, you can now protect your content from being used for Amazon's AI training.

stories.title: Mesh, Automattic’s CRM for everyone, comes to Android
stories.simple_summary: A contacts app called Mesh that uses AI to help manage relationships is now available on Android phones.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Android and want help organizing contacts and remembering details about people, this is a tool you could try.

stories.title: Why Stream ring-maker Sandbar says the future of AI wearables is voice
stories.simple_summary: Companies are making small wearable devices like rings and earbuds that use AI to record your thoughts and turn them into written notes and to-do lists.
stories.why_it_matters: This could be useful for busy people who want to capture ideas hands-free, but it's still new technology.

stories.title: How much time does AI save at work? New Census Bureau data breaks it down.
stories.simple_summary: The U.S. Census Bureau gathered new data showing how much time AI is saving workers in their jobs.
stories.why_it_matters: This will give us a clearer picture of whether AI is actually making work faster and more productive in real life.

stories.title: Lovable confirms new $13.3B valuation, raises another $400M
stories.simple_summary: A startup company called Lovable raised more money and is now valued at over 13 billion dollars because it's making good revenue from its AI products.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Guitar company D’Addario admits that AI music was used in a promotional video
stories.simple_summary: A guitar string and equipment company called D'Addario finally admitted that it secretly used AI-generated music in a promotional video, after denying it for weeks.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows why transparency matters — if you're a business, being honest from the start about using AI saves you from looking dishonest later.
